findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Basis/Submodule.lean:189 `theorem mem_span_iff_repr_mem (m : M) : m ∈ span R (Set.range b) ↔ ∀ i, b.repr m i ∈ Set.range (algebraMap R S)`; `Basis/Basic.lean:264 singleton_repr`; `LinearAlgebra/StdBasis.lean:131 basisFun_repr`; same idiom already used in Mathlib (`Algebra/Module/ZLattice/Covolume.lean:242`) and in TauCeti (`Sl2/IntegralLattice.lean:218-220`).
findings.fix: Delete both private lemmas and use `Module.Basis.mem_span_iff_repr_mem ℤ` with `Basis.singleton_repr` / `Pi.basisFun_repr`, as in `TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/Sl2/IntegralLattice.lean:218` (`rw [Module.Basis.mem_span_iff_repr_mem]; simp only [Pi.basisFun_repr, Set.mem_range, eq_comm]`).
findings.issue: `mem_span_singletonBasis_iff` (line 95) and `mem_span_piBasisFinTwo_iff` (line 106) re-derive Mathlib's `Module.Basis.mem_span_iff_repr_mem` by hand via `Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun` plus `fin_cases`/`choose` plumbing.

findings.evidence: `TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean:243` `ofGramMatrix_carrier ... = Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range b)` — independent of `G`; the four proofs in Examples.lean are `rw [<lattice>, ofGramMatrix_carrier]; exact <one of the two private lemmas>`, pairwise identical.
findings.fix: State one generic lemma next to `ofGramMatrix_carrier`, e.g. `mem_ofGramMatrix_carrier_iff (b : Basis ι ℚ V) (G) (hG) (x) : x ∈ (ofGramMatrix b G hG).carrier ↔ ∀ i, ∃ z : ℤ, (z : ℚ) = b.repr x i`, proved from `ofGramMatrix_carrier` + `Basis.mem_span_iff_repr_mem`, and let the example-level uses (lines 393-414) apply it directly instead of keeping four restatements.
findings.issue: Four parallel public carrier lemmas state one fact: `mem_aOne_carrier_iff` (123) and `mem_negativeAOne_carrier_iff` (130) are the same proposition (both carriers are `span ℤ (Set.range (Basis.singleton (Fin 1) ℚ))`), and `mem_hyperbolicPlane_carrier_iff` (137) and `mem_affineAOne_carrier_iff` (144) are the same proposition (both carriers are `span ℤ (Set.range (Pi.basisFun ℚ (Fin 2)))`). Carrier membership does not depend on the Gram matrix at all.

findings.evidence: `mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Determinant/Basic.lean:814` `det_fin_two_of (a b c d : R) : Matrix.det !![a, b; c, d] = a * d - b * c`; the `!![·;·]` notation for `Matrix.of ![![...]]` is the library's assembly combinator for concrete matrices.
findings.fix: Define them as `!![2]`, `!![-2]`, `!![0, 1; 1, 0]`, `!![2, -2; -2, 2]`; determinant and symmetry proofs then go through Mathlib's literal simp set (`Matrix.det_fin_two_of`, `Matrix.cons_val_*`) without unfolding a private name.
findings.issue: The four Gram matrices (lines 62, 64, 66, 69) are hand-rolled as `fun i j => if i.val = j.val then _ else _` / `fun _ _ => c` instead of Mathlib's matrix-literal constructor, so every downstream proof must `simp only [<matrixName>]` and the definitions do not syntactically match the `!![0, 1; 1, 0]` / `!![2, -2; -2, 2]` matrices advertised in their own docstrings.

summary: The four lattices and their invariants are new material, but the carrier-membership scaffolding re-derives Mathlib's `Basis.mem_span_iff_repr_mem` by hand and then restates the resulting fact four times, once per lattice, although carrier membership depends only on the basis.
